title: fix(plugin-auth): the vendored auth library's client-address source follows server.trustProxy
body:
Fixes #24799

Clause-②: no

## What changed

The vendored auth library (better-auth 1.7.3) resolves a request's client address with its own reader, `getIP` in `@better-auth/core` `utils/ip`. That reader reads request headers only: it never sees the transport's peer address and does not know `server.trustProxy`. `plugin-auth` composed the library without configuring that reader, so the library used its default.

- **The library reads one platform-owned header.** The auth instance's options now always carry `advanced.ipAddress.ipAddressHeaders`, which names the one header the platform owns (`client-address-vendor.ts`, `vendorClientAddressOptions`). No `trustedProxies` is set: the header carries one address the server already decided, never a chain for the library to walk.
- **`handleRequest` writes that header.** `AuthManager.handleRequest` is the one door to the library's HTTP handler. It now rebuilds every request it hands over (`withVendorClientAddress`). Any copy of the header the caller sent is dropped. The address the client-address trust rule established is written in its place. That address comes from `resolveClientAddress` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth/client-address`, after #24795), which is reused here and not copied. When no address was established, nothing is written, and the library is handed no address.
- **Why a header.** The library has no resolver hook. Its option surface is a header list, a proxy-CIDR list for its own walk of a forwarded chain, and an off switch. The off switch also turns the library's rate limiter off, so it cannot express "no address where none exists". A header the platform owns is the one channel through which the rule's answer reaches the library.
- The request is rebuilt from a clone, so the caller's own `Request` stays readable for the auth mount's 404 hand-on. A request that cannot be rebuilt is not handed to the library with a value its caller chose. There is no catch around the rebuild.

Landing: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts` (the composed option and the `handleRequest` write) and a new `client-address-vendor.ts` beside `client-address.ts`. `packages/spec/**`, `packages/runtime/**` and `auth-plugin.ts` are untouched.

## Reachability (the card's first step)

Measured on `origin/main` at `7c2eab929` with the installed better-auth 1.7.3 and `@better-auth/core` 1.7.3, through the real auth mounts (`AuthPlugin.registerAuthRoutes` on Hono, a real `AuthManager`).

Three things read the library's client address in a stock composition:

1. the session row's `ip_address`, and through it the `login` / `logout` audit rows;
2. the `login_failed` / `account_locked` audit address (`signInClientFingerprint` applies the same reader on purpose);
3. the key of the library's own per-address rate limiter (ADR-0069 D2; on by default in production).

`getIP` has four callers in the installed library family: the rate limiter, `createSession`, the captcha plugin, and a re-export. `plugin-auth` composes no captcha.

In both the untrusted-proxy deployment and the trusted-proxy deployment, the address all three answered differed from the address the D5 allow-list judged and the D7 audit stamped. The detail is withheld under the disclosure ruling recorded on #9387.

M4 (does the peer address reach the library?): it does not. The library sees the Fetch `Request` only. The peer reaches `handleRequest` as its `transport.remoteAddress` argument.

## Pins: one per branch, ablation-verified

`client-address-vendor-trust-rule.test.ts` uses the D5/D7 suite's fixture: real mounts, a real `AuthManager`, the peer on `c.env.incoming`. Each pin reads all three seams off one composition: the minted session's `ip_address`, the `login_failed` event's address, and every key the library's limiter consumed (recorded through `rateLimitStorage`). It also reads D7 `last_login_ip` for agreement. Every request also carries the platform-owned header, set by the caller. The refused sign-in asserts `code` + `status` (`INVALID_EMAIL_OR_PASSWORD`, 401).

- `behind a declared trusted proxy, it records and keys on the forwarded client address`
- `without a declared trusted proxy, it records and keys on the connection peer, whatever the request headers say`
- `when the server established no address, it is handed none, whatever the request headers say`. This pin compares against a per-deployment control request that carries no header at all, never against a literal, because the library's own no-address answer depends on its environment.

Ablations ran on `2604658d1` (fix committed first) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`. Each mutation was proven on disk (anchor count 1 to 0, blob changed), and each was restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty. Each "10 passed" / "12 passed" counts the 10 tests the imported fixture module registers.

| # | forbidden behaviour put back | result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | the composed `ipAddress` option removed (library default reader) | 3 failed / 10 passed: all three branches red |
| A2 | the caller's copy of the header not dropped | 1 failed / 12 passed: no-address branch red |
| A3 | the library handed the raw transport peer instead of the established address | 1 failed / 12 passed: trusted-proxy branch red |
| A4 | the forwarded header handed over without declared trust | 2 failed / 11 passed: untrusted-proxy and no-address branches red |
| A5 | the `handleRequest` write removed | 3 failed / 10 passed: all three branches red |

## Tests and gates

All readings below are on head `9d43edafb`, which merges `origin/main` at `9a06f0be0`. That range includes #24846 and #24843, which edit other regions of `auth-manager.ts`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2` exited 0: 171 files, 3273 passed, 10 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` exited 0: `tsc` on src and examples, and `check:test-typecheck` OK (no new debt).
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 70 commands. Each ran with its exit code captured before any pipe, and all 70 exited 0. `--ran` printed: `70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- Two existing suites moved with the behaviour:
  - `auth-manager.test.ts`: the `advanced` passthrough expectations now include the always-composed `ipAddress`.
  - `auth-account-event-audit.test.ts`: the fixture hands its client as the transport peer. It had supplied the client through a forwarded header on a deployment that declares no trusted proxy, which is the behaviour this card removes.
- Repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint` and the full `check:*` farm) are left to CI.

## Acceptance notes

- **Programmatic calls.** A programmatic `auth.api.*` call is handed whatever headers its caller passes. Only `withVendorClientAddress` writes the header, which is documented at the constant and in the changeset. Measured in-repo, no programmatic call reaches an address reader with a client's headers. The calls are `getSession` (reads no address), boot-time `signUpEmail` (no headers) and `requestPasswordReset` (reads no address).
- **The library's own no-address answer.** In production it is no session address and one shared rate-limit bucket, plus a one-time library warning whose remedy names library options that the platform composes itself. In development and test it is a loopback placeholder, and its limiter is off there by default. This is library-owned behaviour, unchanged.
- **IPv6.** The library normalizes IPv6 addresses to their /64 before it keys or stores them. D7 `last_login_ip` stores the established address verbatim. This is pre-existing library behaviour, unchanged.
- **Peerless bridges.** Filed as #24877 (security family; detail withheld under the disclosure ruling recorded on #9387). The bullet was rewritten by the `domain:services` seat 2 at review.
- **Operator note (in the changeset).** Behind a reverse proxy, declare `server.trustProxy`. Otherwise sessions and audit rows record the proxy's address, and the library's per-address rate limit counts every client behind the proxy as one client. This is the same posture the D5 allow-list and the runtime's inbound limiter already take.

Changeset: `.changeset/24799-vendor-client-address-trust.md` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`: patch).
